# GUID-APP-IMPL-009: AWS API Management Implementation Guidance

**← Back to [EAP Home](../../../../README.md) • [Strategy](../../../README.md) • [Guidance](../../README.md) • [Application](../README.md)**

guidance_type: 'implementation'

---

> **AWS API Management Implementation Guidance** — Step-by-step implementation playbook for engineering teams deploying API Management capabilities on AWS. Covers sequencing, decision points, control alignment, and governance evidence requirements. Implements the strategy defined in the [Enterprise API and Microservices Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-api-microservices-strategy.md) and is the companion implementation guide for [REF-APP-API-001](../../../reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md) and [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md).

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#principle-1-reuse-before-reinvent]

#### Principle 1: Reuse Before Reinvent

**Description:** Start from existing standards, patterns, and security guidance.
**Rationale:** Reduces duplication and governance ambiguity.
**Application:** Map all design decisions to existing artifact IDs before implementation.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#principle-2-platform-controls-first]

#### Principle 2: Platform Controls First

**Description:** Implement shared controls (identity, protection, telemetry) before domain-specific API logic.
**Rationale:** Improves consistency and reduces repeated implementation effort.
**Application:** Establish gateway baseline modules and policy templates first.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#principle-3-evidence-by-design]

#### Principle 3: Evidence by Design

**Description:** Produce architecture, security, and operations evidence as part of delivery workflows.
**Rationale:** Simplifies governance review and operational handoff.
**Application:** Include standards mapping and control validation outputs in release artifacts.
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#approach-1-shared-gateway-foundation]

#### Approach 1: Shared Gateway Foundation

**Overview:** Build a reusable platform baseline that domains can consume.
**When to Use:** Multi-domain API programs with common control requirements.
**Implementation:** Provision gateway, identity integration, security controls, and telemetry as shared components.
**Benefits:** Consistent controls and faster onboarding.
**Considerations:** Requires clear ownership and change governance.
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#approach-2-domain-onboarding-waves]

#### Approach 2: Domain Onboarding Waves

**Overview:** Onboard APIs by domain in controlled increments.
**When to Use:** Existing portfolios migrating to centralized API management.
**Implementation:** Prioritize domains, apply baseline controls, validate, then promote.
**Benefits:** Reduced migration risk and clearer rollout visibility.
**Considerations:** Requires compatibility planning for consumer contracts.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#best-practice-1-contract-and-policy-co-validation]

#### Best Practice 1: Contract and Policy Co-Validation

**Description:** Validate API contracts and gateway policies together in CI/CD.
**Rationale:** Prevents contract and policy drift.
**Implementation:** Include standards checks and policy checks in one promotion gate.
**Success Indicators:** Promotion artifacts include both contract and policy evidence.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#best-practice-2-operational-readiness-at-onboarding]

#### Best Practice 2: Operational Readiness at Onboarding

**Description:** Require monitoring, alerting, and audit telemetry before production release.
**Rationale:** Reduces post-release blind spots.
**Implementation:** Include telemetry readiness checks in release criteria.
**Success Indicators:** Runbooks and dashboards exist before production cutover.
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#pitfall-1-gateway-only-thinking]

#### Pitfall 1: Gateway-Only Thinking

**Description:** Treating API management as routing only.
**Impact:** Missing lifecycle governance and developer onboarding controls.
**Prevention:** Use platform model that covers runtime plus lifecycle control plane.
**Mitigation:** Add control-plane workflows and portal onboarding patterns.
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#pitfall-2-incomplete-security-integration]

#### Pitfall 2: Incomplete Security Integration

**Description:** Applying gateway controls without identity and policy integration.
**Impact:** Inconsistent authn/authz enforcement.
**Prevention:** Align implementation with referenced security guidance from day one.
**Mitigation:** Re-baseline policy integration and revalidate access paths.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#preparation-steps]

#### Preparation Steps

1. **Step 1**: Define API scope and consumer categories for the target domain.

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: API inventory and ownership model
    - Key activities and tasks: categorize APIs by exposure type (internal vs external) and lifecycle stage; use [STD-APP-API-003](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-003-internal-external-api-guidelines.md) for classification criteria
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: prioritized onboarding scope with explicit internal/external classification

2. **Step 2**: Classify each API by traffic pattern (North-South or East-West) per [STD-APP-API-004](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-004-north-south-east-west-apis.md).

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: API scope from Step 1
    - Key activities and tasks: for North-South APIs, onboard to API Gateway; for East-West APIs, first determine the API type (REST, HTTP/WebSocket, or native gRPC/event API not proxyable by Amazon API Gateway), since the compliant control path differs by type — **REST APIs**: apply the approved decision branch required by [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) and deploy a Private API Gateway (endpoint type `PRIVATE`, VPC Endpoint-only) as the mandatory control-plane baseline (REQ-APIGW-01/03/04); **HTTP or WebSocket APIs**: these support only Regional (internet-routable) endpoints and cannot deploy a `PRIVATE` API Gateway, so this is a genuine, unresolved SBB/technical-capability gap per [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md) Requirement 5 — no ALB, other private frontend, or VPC Link/NLB integration is authorized as a sanctioned substitute for the SBB's control; re-platform the boundary as a REST API using the `PRIVATE` endpoint type wherever the API's actual requirements permit it, and track any API that cannot be re-platformed as an open compliance gap through Security Architecture's SBB exception process rather than a self-approved workaround; **native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy** (e.g., APIs contracted via `.proto` or AsyncAPI per Step 3 below): the AWS-specific gateway-interception mandate in GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB does not apply to these APIs — apply the platform-neutral Gateway vs. Mesh decision framework in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) instead, consistent with [GUID-APP-IMPL-010](./GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#q9-when-do-i-use-api-management-vs-service-mesh) Q9, which permits mesh-only internal communication where appropriate for this category. For all East-West API types, layer service mesh per STD-APP-API-006 as a complementary control where mTLS or fine-grained service identity is additionally needed; document the decision
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: N-S/E-W mapping documented; every East-West API has a control path addressed by type — REST APIs have the mandatory Private API Gateway baseline deployed; HTTP/WebSocket APIs either have the `PRIVATE`-endpoint REST re-platform completed or the unresolved SBB gap logged and tracked through Security Architecture's exception process; native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy have a documented Gateway-or-Mesh decision per STD-APP-API-006 — optionally layered with service mesh where mTLS or fine-grained service identity is additionally required; no East-West API is excluded from this decision, and service mesh alone is never substituted for the mandatory gateway baseline where that baseline is achievable

3. **Step 3**: Register all in-scope APIs in the API catalog before implementation begins.

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: a style-appropriate API contract for each API — OpenAPI 3.x for REST, `.proto`/GraphQL SDL/AsyncAPI for other styles (contract-first per [STD-APP-API-001](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md) and Q11 of [GUID-APP-IMPL-010](./GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#q11-is-openapi-the-standard))
    - Key activities and tasks: commit the API contract to source control; register in enterprise developer portal or internal catalog
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: API catalog entries with owner, type, lifecycle stage, and spec reference

4. **Step 4**: Map architecture controls to referenced standards and guidance.

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: current design and policy artifacts
    - Key activities and tasks: produce standards/patterns/guidance mapping
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: validated implementation baseline
page_texts.52:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#execution-steps]

#### Execution Steps

1. **Step 1**: Deploy baseline gateway, identity, and security integrations.

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: approved baseline configurations
    - Key activities and tasks: apply IaC and policy templates
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: platform-ready API ingress model

2. **Step 2**: Configure OpenTelemetry instrumentation in Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services (proposed, pending [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) ratification — currently `status: draft`; teams are encouraged to instrument proactively ahead of ratification).

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: OTel Collector deployed on target cluster; STD-APP-MON-002 (proposed/pending ratification)
    - Key activities and tasks: instrument each service with the OTel SDK (traces, metrics, structured logs); configure Collector to route signals to Dynatrace (primary enterprise APM); Lambda/ECS backends outside Kubernetes/EKS scope use the CloudWatch/X-Ray AWS-native baseline instead; validate telemetry flow
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: once STD-APP-MON-002 completes ratification, OTel instrumentation active in all Kubernetes/EKS-deployed in-scope services before production promotion; Lambda/ECS services follow the CloudWatch/X-Ray baseline instead

3. **Step 3**: Onboard domain APIs with contract and policy validation.

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: API definitions and deployment pipeline
    - Key activities and tasks: run standards and policy checks before promotion
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: controlled API publication
page_texts.53:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#validation-steps]

#### Validation Steps

1. **Step 1**: Verify runtime controls, telemetry, and governance evidence.

    - Required inputs and prerequisites: deployed APIs and monitoring setup
    - Key activities and tasks: execute readiness checks and review artifacts
    - Expected outputs and outcomes: publish-ready operating baseline
page_texts.55:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#decision-point-1-shared-vs-domain-gateway-segmentation]

#### Decision Point 1: Shared vs Domain Gateway Segmentation

**Context:** Determine gateway tenancy and ownership model.
**Options:** Shared enterprise gateway, domain-segmented gateways, or hybrid.
**Criteria:** Governance consistency, domain autonomy, operational complexity.
**Recommendation:** Use shared baseline controls with optional domain segmentation when required by context.
page_texts.56:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#decision-point-2-api-migration-sequence]

#### Decision Point 2: API Migration Sequence

**Context:** Determine migration order for existing APIs.
**Options:** Critical-first, low-risk-first, or domain-wave rollout.
**Criteria:** Consumer impact, contract compatibility, operational readiness.
**Recommendation:** Use domain-wave rollout with explicit validation gates.
page_texts.57:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#tools-and-techniques]

### Tools and Techniques

| Tool Category | Tool Name | Purpose | Usage Guidelines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway Platform | Amazon API Gateway | API ingress and policy enforcement for North-South APIs, and the mandatory East-West private control-plane baseline (`PRIVATE` endpoint type) for internal service-to-service APIs per [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md) Requirement 5 | Deploy via controlled IaC and release gates; East-West onboarding follows Step 2 |
| Security Controls | AWS WAF and identity integration | Threat protection and access control | Align with referenced security guidance |
| Application Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK + OTel Collector | Application-level traces, metrics, and structured logs per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) | Proposed for Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification (currently `status: draft`); configure before production deployment once ratified |
| Observability Backends | CloudWatch, CloudTrail, SIEM integration | AWS-native compute resource metrics/logs (Lambda, ECS) and management-plane telemetry, plus SIEM integration; Dynatrace is the primary APM destination for OTel-routed application telemetry | Enable before production cutover; OTel Collector routes Kubernetes/EKS application telemetry to Dynatrace |

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#examples-and-use-cases]

## Examples and Use Cases

> **Note:** The scenarios and case studies below are illustrative — they describe expected outcomes from applying this guidance, not outcomes observed at a specific cited implementation. No traceable real-world implementation evidence currently exists anywhere in this artifact suite (see [GUID-APP-IMPL-011](./GUID-APP-IMPL-011-aws-api-management-platform-guidance.md) Change History, v1.0.9/v1.0.8). Unlike a Pattern, this Guidance does not require proven, real-world adoption evidence; the entries below are presented as expected-outcome illustrations to aid onboarding, not as case-study evidence.
page_texts.64:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#scenario-1-partner-api-onboarding]

#### Scenario 1: Partner API Onboarding

**Context:** Domain publishes partner-facing APIs on AWS.
**Challenge:** Need consistent access control, protection, and telemetry.
**Application:** Apply shared controls, domain onboarding workflow, and evidence pack.
**Expected Outcome:** Controlled partner exposure with architecture and security traceability.
**Lessons Applied:** Shared controls reduce implementation variance.
page_texts.65:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#scenario-2-internal-api-governance]

#### Scenario 2: Internal API Governance

**Context:** Internal service APIs require standardized governance.
**Challenge:** Multiple teams with differing implementation practices.
**Application:** Use shared baseline and staged onboarding approach.
**Expected Outcome:** Consistent policy and observability posture.
**Lessons Applied:** Contract and policy co-validation is essential.
page_texts.67:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#use-case-1-new-domain-launch]

#### Use Case 1: New Domain Launch

**Scenario Description:** New domain launches APIs using enterprise AWS baseline.
**Context:** No prior domain-specific gateway implementation.
**Guidance Application:** Execute full foundation-to-onboarding sequence.
**Adaptations:** Adjust gateway segmentation model for domain boundaries.
**Success Factors:** Early standards mapping and evidence preparation.
page_texts.68:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#use-case-2-legacy-api-migration]

#### Use Case 2: Legacy API Migration

**Scenario Description:** Existing APIs migrate into managed platform model.
**Context:** Consumer contracts and operations already in place.
**Guidance Application:** Use phased migration with compatibility validation.
**Adaptations:** Add temporary coexistence controls where needed.
**Success Factors:** Clear migration sequencing and runtime verification.
page_texts.70:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#case-study-1-platform-first-api-program-enablement]

#### Case Study 1: Platform-First API Program Enablement

**Background:** Teams need fast, consistent AWS API onboarding.
**Challenge:** Prior implementations vary by team and project.
**Solution Approach:** Build a shared control baseline, then onboard by domain.
**Implementation Details:** Integrate gateway, identity, security, and telemetry controls into reusable templates.
**Expected Results:** Improved conformance and reduced architecture review rework.
**Analysis:** Platform-first sequencing is expected to improve delivery consistency; this has not yet been observed at a specific cited implementation.
page_texts.72:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md#implementation-lessons]

#### Implementation Lessons

- Shared controls should be implemented before large-scale API onboarding.
- Governance evidence is easier to produce when embedded in delivery workflows.
- Domain onboarding is most effective when rollout waves are small and validated.
